facts.claim: "Grown (Live from Piomingo)" is a six-song live EP by Peytan Porter, released May 10, 2024. The Apple Music listing credits the label as Warner Chappell Nashville / Jody Williams Songs / Red Light Management.

The live versions were released as a video series, with one live video per song on the studio EP. The final installment was a live video of "Run the Radio", and the live versions reached streaming services on May 10, 2024.
"Grown" was written by Peytan Porter, Steve Moakler and Mark Trussell.
Porter said she wrote about half of "Grown" herself, then brought it to Steve Moakler and Mark Trussell to finish together.
The song is about finding peace and pride in the lives we build, even when they aren't what we expected. It also looks for beauty in silver linings.

The song centers on Porter realizing that some of the hardest parts of her journey came at the right time. It also speaks to how easily she compares her life to friends and family who are in a different phase.
The studio EP "Grown" came out March 1, 2024. Billboard called it her sophomore EP, described it as having gauzy, Laurel Canyon-style vibes, and named her its March Country Rookie of the Month.
Porter co-wrote all six tracks on the EP. Press describes an earthy sound that comes from her small-town upbringing in Dawsonville, Georgia.
Her debut project, "In My Head", earned 10 million streams. She had 50 million TikTok views at the time of the EP announcement.

Porter is a Dawsonville, Georgia native. She signed a publishing deal with Jody Williams Songs and Warner Chappell Music, and her TikTok following helped launch her recording career. Her debut record is "In My Head".

draft:
Two things fill **Grown (Live from Piomingo)**: an acoustic guitar picking out arpeggios in a clean, bright tone, and Peytan Porter's voice, clear and unhurried, riding on top. Nothing else crowds in. The tempo leans back instead of pushing, the playing has a raw, unpolished edge, and the whole performance feels like it's happening a few feet away. For a song about making peace with where you've ended up, that bareness makes the case. There's no band to stand behind.

Porter has described the song as being about finding peace and pride in the life you've built, even when it isn't the one you pictured, and about looking for beauty in the silver linings. The more tender detail sits underneath. She's said it came from realizing that some of the hardest stretches of her journey arrived at the right time, and from how easily she measures her own life against friends and family who are in a different phase. Anyone who has quietly kept score against people who seem to be hitting their milestones on schedule knows that feeling. What makes the idea land is that the pride and the comparing don't cancel each other out. You can be settled in your life and still glance sideways at everyone else's. The song's premise leaves room for both.

Porter wrote about half of it on her own, then brought it to Steve Moakler and Mark Trussell to finish together. It's the title track of her sophomore EP, released in March 2024. She co-wrote all six songs on that record, and press has tied its earthy sound to her small-town upbringing in Dawsonville, Georgia. Billboard heard gauzy, Laurel Canyon-style vibes on the studio versions and named her its Country Rookie of the Month. The live take came out of a video series, one performance for each song on the EP, later gathered as a six-song live EP. Whatever haze the studio added is gone here, and the song holds up without it.

That puts it in the Nashville singer-songwriter tradition with its roots in folk-country. Porter has said Kacey Musgraves' *Same Trailer Different Park* made her feel seen. Musgraves is a useful reference point for a writer who wants hometown plainness and emotional honesty to sit in the same song. Porter built her early audience on TikTok, where her debut project, *In My Head*, found millions of listeners. A guitar-and-voice performance like this one suits that path, since it's meant to reach people one at a time.

It sticks because it gives you permission to be proud of a life that didn't follow the plan, without asking you to stop wondering about the one that did.

factCheck.claim: Porter's voice is clear and unhurried
factCheck.note: All three passes say clear; passes 1 and 3 say relaxed or smooth delivery.

factCheck.claim: Nothing else crowds in / there's no band to stand behind
factCheck.note: Pass 2 hears a bass guitar. Passes 1 and 3 hear none. The absolute claim is not safe, so it was dropped and the description now sticks to guitar and voice.

factCheck.claim: Tempo leans back; raw, unpolished edge; feels close and intimate
factCheck.note: Moderate-to-slow, relaxed tempo (all passes). Raw and unpolished (passes 2 and 3). Intimate (passes 1 and 2).
